children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose on Wednesday for a fourth consecutive session to close at a two-month high, led by gains in chipmakers on an AI rally.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 63.01 points, or 0.90%, at 7,080.92, its highest closing level since July 23.
** South Korean financial markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for Chuseok holidays.
** The index ended the week 2.7% higher, after falling 0.2% last week.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 3.25% and peer SK Hynix
gained 1.20%, tracking an overnight rally in US peers.
** During the session, the index erased early gains of 1.9% and briefly turned lower on caution ahead of holidays, before rebounding.
** "There was profit-taking pressure from retail and foreign investors ahead of holidays, but AI semiconductor momentum remained strong," said Lee Kyoung-min, an analyst at Daishin Securities.
** The Nasdaq
notched a record-high close on Tuesday, lifted by Micron Technology
and other AI-related stocks, while the S&P 500
hovered just below a record high as oil prices traded around $100 per barrel.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
climbed 0.29%, while Hyundai Motor
and sister automaker Kia Corp
were down 1.94% and 2.62%, respectively.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.89%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 1.80%.
** Of the total 912 traded issues, 311 shares advanced, while 548 declined.
** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 510.1 billion won ($375.89 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,358.4 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.14% lower than its previous close at 1,356.5.
** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.08 point to 102.37.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) edged up 0.2 basis points to 4.010%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 6.7 basis points to 4.397%.
